criteria.reasoning: The memo reports line 11, column (f) as “$3,671,600,” and its computation lists contributions of $3,590,300 plus interest and dividends of $81,300. This matches the criterion’s required five-year total support.

The memo places “Gross receipts from related activities” totaling $454,400 on line 12 and explicitly says these receipts “are not in support” and “not part of public or total support.” It identifies workshop fees, guided trip fees, and the $256,000 Kettle County monitoring contract, which it describes as a fee for services, not a grant.

The memo never mentions the $182,000 realized gain or says it is excluded because gains on capital-asset sales are not support. It reports line 11 total support as $3,671,600 without addressing the gain, so the criterion fails.
The memo states, “Limit: 2% × $3,671,600 (line 11, column (f)) = $73,432,” which is the required five-year limit figure.

The memo says Benedict Sarkis’s five-year total is $50,000, “Under the limit on his five-year total,” and counts “$50,000” as public support with “$0” excess. It does not apply the 2% limit year by year to him.

The memo applies the 2% limit to Oregon DEQ, stating it counts $73,432 and has $86,568 of excess. The criterion fails if the limit is applied to either funder, even though the memo counts Upper Alder’s full $135,000.

The memo identifies Hollins-Pryor Family Foundation as a private foundation and states that the 2% limit applies because it is “not a publicly supported organization.” It counts $73,432 as public support and excludes $151,568, rather than treating it like the community foundation.
The memo reports line 6 public support as “$1,174,028,” not the required $1,260,596. It also explicitly limits the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, matching a listed failing treatment.
The memo reports the line 14 public support percentage as “31.98%.” The criterion requires 34.33% (or 34.3% to one decimal) and explicitly identifies 31.98% as a failing result.

The memo plainly concludes, “No — on the 2025 computation we fall short of the 33⅓% test,” and says the Council “would have to rely on the 10% facts-and-circumstances test.” This directly meets the criterion’s FAIL conditions.

The memo says the result is “31.98%” and “about 1.4 percentage points below the line,” with public support “$49,839 short” of one-third. The criterion requires a result about one percentage point above the threshold (34.33%) or $36,729 above it, so the stated margin does not satisfy it.

The memo recommends treating “Ms. Ostrander's 2025 gift of $455,000 as an unusual grant” and says removing it would raise the percentage above one-third. The criterion explicitly fails if the memo recommends reclassifying any donor’s gifts as unusual grants.
